subject: SIG request: TLS forward secrecy ciphers + ephemeral key rotation samples
messages:
From: Eva Thompson <eva.thompson@crestbank.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-01T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Request: TLS PFS cipher inventory + ephemeral rotation samples for SIG

Mina,

As part of our SIG review for the upcoming audit window, we need a short evidence set covering the TLS configurations that support forward secrecy and a sampling of ephemeral key rotation records for the last 30 days. Specifically: 
- An inventory (CSV) of TLS listener configurations and enabled ciphers/cipher-suites (include OpenSSL notation where possible).
- A sampling of ephemeral key rotation logs (ephemeral keys / session ticket rotation / TLS session resumption events) covering at least 3 distinct hosts or load balancers.
- Cryptographic hashes for any files you deliver and a short README describing how the samples were generated/exported.

Can you provide these artifacts or point me to a secure transfer method? Target for our SIG reviewer is COB 2026-12-03 if possible.

Thanks,
Eva Thompson
Senior InfoSec Analyst, CrestBank
security@crestbank.com

--
Note: Please redact any tenant-identifying headers if sensitive.

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Eva Thompson <eva.thompson@crestbank.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-01T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: TLS PFS cipher inventory + ephemeral rotation samples for SIG

Eva — thanks for the clear list. We'll assemble a limited evidence packet that matches the SIG scope and avoid tenant-identifying data as requested. Quick clarifications before we start: 
1) For the "sampling of ephemeral key rotation logs" — do you want raw system logs (we can provide sanitized extracts) or a structured CSV of rotation events (timestamp, host, rotation_type, key_id_hash)?
2) Preferred transfer: we can (a) upload to the SFTP endpoint you provide, (b) share a Google Drive folder with restricted access, or (c) deliver via an encrypted ZIP with SHA256 hashes in email. Which is best for CrestBank?

I'll coordinate collection with infra; Ben, Neha — can you help with the exports? 

Mina Haddad
Security & Compliance Manager | Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Eva Thompson <eva.thompson@crestbank.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-02T08:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: TLS PFS cipher inventory + ephemeral rotation samples for SIG

Eva / Mina — attaching the artifacts we discussed. Transfer summary below and a short note on scope. 

Attachments included (stubs):
- pfs-cipher-inventory.csv (CSV: host, listener, tls_version, cipher_suite_openssl, enabled_preference)
- ephemeral-rotation-snapshot-202611.zip (ZIP: sanitized rotation event extracts for three load balancer nodes; internal tenant IDs redacted)
- README-transfer-instructions.txt (short notes on export method and SHA256 hashes)

We generated the rotation samples by sampling ingress/load-balancer TLS handshakes and session ticket rekeys from 2026-11-01 to 2026-11-30. Each rotation event row includes a UTC timestamp, hostname, rotation_type (ticket_rekey/session_rekey), and the SHA256 hash of the exported key identifier (no raw key material). The ZIP also contains a verification manifest (manifest.sha256). 

Transfer method: uploaded to CrestBank SFTP at sftp://uploads.crestbank-secure.net/redwood/mina_haddad (please confirm you can access). If preferred, we can alternatively share the Drive folder link.

Notes / caveats:
- We do not export private key material or any full session keys — only redacted/sampled rotation metadata and identifiers hashed with SHA256.
- Cipher names are reported in OpenSSL format where available. For legacy listeners we include TLS version and note of whether PFS is enforced by policy.

Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
Attachments: pfs-cipher-inventory.csv (attachment), ephemeral-rotation-snapshot-202611.zip (attachment), README-transfer-instructions.txt (attachment)

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Eva Thompson <eva.thompson@crestbank.com>
Date: 2026-12-02T09:00:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: TLS PFS cipher inventory + ephemeral rotation samples for SIG

Thanks Ben — that looks good. A couple of operational points for the reviewer: 
- The SHA256 hashes in the README correspond to the filenames in the ZIP; please validate the manifest before opening.
- The CSV includes an "enforcement" column (yes/no) showing whether the load balancer is configured to disallow non-PFS suites. For older tenants we have a note of scheduled mitigation windows.

Neha — can you confirm the samples meet our redaction standard (no tenant identifiers, user IPs trimmed)?

Mina

Team — confirmed receipt of the SFTP upload and the three attachments. Quick follow-up: can you also include KEK wrapping/unwrapping audit entries for the TLS edge devices (a small sample, same redaction rules)? Our SIG reviewer wants to see evidence that KEK operations are recorded alongside rotation events. If you can drop a short CSV with those events in the same folder (or reply with a manifest link), that would close out the artifact ask on our side.

I'll review by Friday 2026-12-04 and let you know if anything else is needed. Appreciate the fast turnaround.

Thanks,
Eva
